summary: README's "On a fork's pull request" section describes a failure sequence the code no longer produces: it asserts the governance-token secret is what stops the run first, and that the caller's own checkout fails with `Repository not found` because the governance-repo checkout is never reached. The actual workflow now checks the key, unconditionally, before either checkout runs at all, and reports a different message entirely: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not available to this workflow.`.

evidence.text:
Secrets are not passed to workflows triggered from a fork, so **both** arrive
blank — and it is the governance token, not the key, that stops the run first.
The checkout of this repository fails with `Repository not found` before the
runner is ever built, so nothing reaches the code that would report a missing
key.

PR #1's own body (verevoir/aigency-governance#1, read via read_pull_request in this pass) independently names this as one of four documentation findings fixed at that same commit. Full before/after diff in diff.txt (hunk 1).
